description:
PROBLEM TYPE: LP

PROBLEM INFO:

- A small electric utility operates \var{P} power plants to supply electricity to \var{C} cities.
- Each power plant has a capacity of \var{supply_{p}} million kwh.
- Each city has a peak demand of \var{demand_{c}} million kwh, which must be met at the same time.
- Power plant \var{p} can send electricity to city \var{c} at a transmission cost of \var{transmission_{p,c}} $/million kwh.

INPUT FORMAT: 

{
    "supply": [supply_{p} for p in 1, ..., P],
    "demand": [demand_{c} for c in 1, ..., C],
    "transmission_costs": [[transmission_{p,c} for c in 1, ..., C] for p in 1, ..., P]
}

OBJECTIVE: How much electricity should each power plant send to each city to minimize the total transmission cost?

OUTPUT INFO:

- the amount of electricity power plant \var{p} sends to city \var{c} as \var{send_{p,c}} million kwh.
- \var{total_cost} displays the total transmission cost for the utility.

OUTPUT FORMAT:

{
    "send": [[send_{p,c} for c in 1, ..., C] for p in 1, ..., P],
    "total_cost": total_cost
}

Supply.definition: Electricity supply capacity of power plant p

TransmissionCosts.definition: Transmission cost from power plant p to city c

objective.description: "The goal is to minimize the total transmission cost of sending electricity from power plants to cities while meeting all supply and demand constraints."

constraints.description: For each power plant p, the total electricity sent to all cities cannot exceed its supply capacity: sum over c of send_{p,c} <= supply_{p}
For each city c, the total electricity received from all power plants must meet its demand: sum over p of send_{p,c} = demand_{c}
All electricity shipment variables must be non-negative: send_{p,c} >= 0 for all p, c

send.definition: Amount of electricity sent from power plant p to city c (in million kwh)
